mainTopic: Hidden sheaves and מין במינו, then the laws of עגלה ערופה: which bodies and cities are included, how and from where to measure, and the ceremony itself.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a side discussion about a sheaf placed on top of another sheaf and then forgotten. The גמרא concludes that, for רבי יהודה, even something covered by its own kind (מין במינו) counts as hidden (טמון). Next, a ברייתא reads each word of the פסוק about עגלה ערופה as a limit. רבי אלעזר answers that only the extra word 'חלל' creates a limit. The גמרא then explains the משנה's rules: there is no עגלה ערופה near the border or near a city of mostly נכרים, and a city with no בית דין is skipped when measuring. A new משנה follows. It covers a body found exactly between two cities, why ירושלים is excluded, a head and body found apart, and where on the body the measuring starts. The גמרא explains each of these, including רבי יצחק's view that the head-and-body dispute is really about burying a מת מצוה. The amud ends with another משנה describing the ceremony itself: the heifer, the strong stream, the breaking of the neck, and the elders' declaration that they did not neglect the traveler.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a sheaf placed on another sheaf
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא about a sheaf put on top of another sheaf and forgotten. The ת״ק and רבי שמעון בן יהודה disagree about which sheaf is שכחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You already learned this: A man picked up a sheaf to bring it to town, put it on top of another sheaf, and forgot them. The lower sheaf is שכחה, and the upper one is not. רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון: neither is שכחה. The lower one is hidden, and the upper one is 'floating.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as a source for whether something lying on top of its own kind counts as hidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree the upper sheaf is not שכחה. They argue only about the lower sheaf. The ת״ק says it is שכחה, while רבי שמעון בן יהודה says it is exempt because it is hidden (טמון) under the other sheaf.

keyTerms.meaning: A forgotten sheaf, which must be left for the poor
Floating, not resting directly on the ground of the field

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sheaves. Both sides agree the upper sheaf is not שכחה. The whole argument is about the lower one.

phrases.english: You learned it:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is pointing to a ברייתא that helps with the question it was just discussing.

phrases.english: A sheaf that he held in order to take it to the city,
and he placed it on top of another sheaf and forgot it —
the lower one is a forgotten sheaf
and the upper one is not a forgotten sheaf.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
Neither of them is a forgotten sheaf,
the lower one because it is hidden,
and the upper one because it is floating.

steps.raayaObject: Whether something lying on its own kind counts as hidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a sheaf placed on top of another sheaf

steps.title: Assumption: both sides follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא assumes both תנאים in the ברייתא agree with רבי יהודה that a hidden sheaf is not שכחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They assumed that these תנאים hold like רבי יהודה, who says that the word 'in the field' comes to exclude a hidden sheaf.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא states an assumption that will be used in the next step to explain the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה learns from the word 'בשדה' that only a sheaf lying openly in the field can be שכחה, so a hidden sheaf is excluded. If both sides accept this rule, their argument must be about something else.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנאים, the sages of the משנה era
'In the field', a word in the פסוק about שכחה

phrases.english: They assumed that these Tannaim
hold in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda,
who says: "In the field" — this excludes a hidden sheaf.
phrases.notes: דברים 24:19

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up an assumption about the ברייתא from step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both תנאים are assumed to agree with רבי יהודה that a hidden sheaf is not שכחה

steps.title: Suggestion: they argue whether מין במינו is hidden
steps.stepSummary: Based on the assumption, the גמרא suggests the argument is whether a sheaf under its own kind counts as hidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it that they argue about this: one Sage holds that a thing among its own kind counts as hidden, and the other holds that it does not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the ברייתא: the two sides must disagree about whether מין במינו counts as טמון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If everyone agrees that hidden sheaves are exempt, the only open question is whether a sheaf under another sheaf counts as hidden. רבי שמעון בן יהודה would say yes, so it is exempt. The ת״ק would say no, so it is שכחה.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that…? (introduces a suggested proof)
A thing among its own kind

phrases.english: Is it not that they disagree about this:

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר סָבַר: מִין בְּמִינוֹ הָוֵי טָמוּן,
phrases.english: one Sage holds: a thing among its own kind counts as hidden,
and the other Sage holds: it does not count as hidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the assumption in step 2 to define the argument
steps.raayaObject: That מין במינו being טמון is a matter of dispute
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא, read as following רבי יהודה

steps.title: Rejection: everyone agrees מין במינו is hidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Everyone may agree מין במינו is hidden, and the argument is really the old מחלוקת of רבי יהודה and רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. If they held like רבי יהודה, then everyone would agree that a thing among its own kind is hidden. Here they are arguing the same dispute as רבי יהודה and the רבנן. The רבנן of the ברייתא follow those רבנן, and רבי שמעון בן יהודה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. The dispute does not have to be about מין במינו at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא drops the assumption that both sides follow רבי יהודה. Instead, the ת״ק holds like the רבנן, who say even a hidden sheaf can be שכחה. רבי שמעון בן יהודה holds like רבי יהודה, who exempts a hidden sheaf. Both may agree that a sheaf under another sheaf counts as hidden.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא does not prove there is a dispute about מין במינו. It may simply repeat the argument between רבי יהודה and רבנן about hidden sheaves.

phrases.aramaic: לָא, אִי כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סְבִירָא לְהוּ,
phrases.english: No, if they held in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מִין בְּמִינוֹ הָוֵי טָמוּן,
phrases.english: then everyone agrees that a thing among its own kind counts as hidden,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבָּנַן קָמִיפַּלְגִי,
phrases.english: and here they disagree over the dispute of Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis,
so the Rabbis follow the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: The first 'Rabbis' are the ones in this ברייתא. The second are the ones who argue with רבי יהודה about hidden sheaves.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda follows Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, אִי כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סְבִירָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 3
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the ברייתא shows a dispute about מין במינו
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The assumption that both תנאים follow רבי יהודה is not necessary

steps.title: Challenge: why use a sheaf on another sheaf?
steps.stepSummary: If they just argue about hidden sheaves in general, why did the ברייתא use a case of one sheaf on another, and not a sheaf in dirt or pebbles?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why specifically on top of another sheaf? The same argument would apply even to a sheaf hidden in dirt and pebbles!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading from step 4. Why would the ברייתא pick this particular case?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the argument is simply whether hidden sheaves are exempt, a plainer example would be a sheaf covered with dirt. Choosing the case of sheaf-on-sheaf seems to point to something special about מין במינו.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, מַאי אִירְיָא עַל גַּבֵּי חֲבֵירוֹ?
phrases.english: If so, why specifically on top of another sheaf?
The same would be true even in dirt and pebbles!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מַאי אִירְיָא עַל גַּבֵּי חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading offered in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא is just the general dispute about hidden sheaves
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A general dispute would be better shown with a sheaf hidden in dirt. The choice of sheaf-on-sheaf seems purposeful.

steps.title: Answer: to show how far רבי יהודה goes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees the dispute covers all hidden sheaves. The sheaf-on-sheaf case was chosen to show that רבי יהודה treats even מין במינו as hidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. The ברייתא chose this case to show you the strength of רבי יהודה's view: he says that even a thing among its own kind counts as hidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It admits the point, and explains that this case teaches something new about רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think only a sheaf under a different material, like dirt, counts as hidden. The ברייתא picked the harder case to show that רבי יהודה exempts even a sheaf hidden under its own kind. All the more so, he exempts a sheaf hidden in dirt.

keyTerms.meaning: To show you the strength (how far the opinion goes)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's case of sheaf-on-sheaf teaches that, according to רבי יהודה, even something covered by its own kind (מין במינו) is considered טמון.

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so,
and it was taught this way to show you the strength of Rabbi Yehuda's view,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ מִין בְּמִינוֹ הָוֵי טָמוּן.
phrases.english: who says: even a thing among its own kind counts as hidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי, וּלְהוֹדִיעֲךָ כֹּחוֹ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concedes the point and explains the choice of case as a teaching device
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a sheaf covered by a different material, like dirt, would count as hidden
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יהודה, even a sheaf covered by another sheaf (מין במינו) counts as hidden

steps.title: A ברייתא reads each word of the פסוק as a limit on עגלה ערופה
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא learns five limits from the words of the פסוק. רבי אלעזר says that if the person was killed by a weapon, they always break the calf's neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'Slain' means killed by a weapon, not strangled. 'Slain' means already dead, not still twitching. 'In the land' means on the ground, not hidden in a pile of stones. 'Lying' means on the ground, not hanging on a tree. 'In the field' means on land, not floating on water. רבי אלעזר says: in all these cases, if he was killed by a weapon, they break the calf's neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that uses the words of the פסוק to decide which dead bodies require עגלה ערופה. רבי אלעזר disagrees with most of these limits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא treats every word of the פסוק (חלל, באדמה, נופל, בשדה) as an exact requirement. רבי אלעזר keeps only one requirement: the person must be a חלל, killed by a weapon. Where the body was found makes no difference to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone killed, here meaning killed by a weapon
Twitching, still in the death throes
Hidden in a pile of stones
They break the neck of the calf (do עגלה ערופה)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר does not reject everything the ברייתא says. He agrees the person must be a חלל, killed by a weapon. He only disagrees with the limits about where the body was found.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"Slain" — but not strangled,
phrases.notes: These words come from the פסוק in דברים 21:1.

phrases.english: "Slain" — but not twitching,
"In the land" — but not hidden in a pile of stones,
"Lying" — but not hanging on a tree,
"In the field" — but not floating on the surface of the water.
Rabbi Elazar says: In all of these cases,
if he was slain by a weapon, they break the calf's neck.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the main topic of עגלה ערופה after the side discussion about hidden sheaves in steps 1-6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, each word of the פסוק limits the case: killed by a weapon, already dead, on the ground, lying, and in the field. According to רבי אלעזר, only 'killed by a weapon' is needed.

steps.title: The Sages challenge רבי אלעזר from the strangled case
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים point out that רבי אלעזר also excludes a strangled person. If he reads 'חלל' exactly, he should read the other words exactly too.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יוסי בר יהודה said that the Sages said to רבי אלעזר: Don't you agree that if he was strangled and left in a garbage heap, they do not break the calf's neck? So you agree that 'slain' means not strangled. Then here too, 'in the land' should mean not hidden in a pile, 'lying' should mean not hanging on a tree, and 'in the field' should mean not floating on water.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים attack רבי אלעזר using something he himself agrees with. He reads the word 'חלל' as a strict limit, so why not the other words?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר agrees that a strangled person does not get עגלה ערופה, which means he reads 'חלל' exactly. The חכמים say he is being inconsistent. If one word of the פסוק is a limit, then 'באדמה', 'נופל' and 'בשדה' should be limits too.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too, the same should apply

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda said:
They said to Rabbi Elazar:
Don't you agree
that if he was strangled and left lying in a garbage heap
they do not break the calf's neck?
So we see that "slain" means not strangled.
phrases.notes: They mean that even you, רבי אלעזר, read this word as an exact limit.

phrases.english: Here too, "in the land" should mean not hidden in a pile of stones,
"lying" should mean not hanging on a tree,
and "in the field" should mean not floating on the water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, אִי אַתָּה מוֹדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעזר's position from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's view that where the body was found does not matter
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He reads 'חלל' as an exact limit to exclude a strangled person. To be consistent, he should also read the other words of the פסוק as exact limits.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: 'חלל' is written an extra time
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that he excludes a strangled person only because 'חלל' is repeated in the פסוקים. The other words are not repeated, so they are not limits.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר answers: the word 'slain' is written an extra time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי אלעזר's answer to the challenge in step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר says a single word of the פסוק does not automatically create a limit. 'חלל' is different because the תורה writes it a second time, and that extra mention teaches us to exclude a strangled person. 'באדמה', 'נופל' and 'בשדה' have no extra mention, so they teach no limit.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא reads every word of the פסוק as a limit on עגלה ערופה. רבי אלעזר learns a limit only from the extra 'חלל', so he excludes a strangled person but not a body that was hidden, hanging, or floating.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar answers:
"Slain" is written an extra time.
phrases.notes: The second mention is in דברים 21:2.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the word 'חלל' from the other words because it appears an extra time
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים thought that if רבי אלעזר reads one word of the פסוק exactly, he must read all of them exactly.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the extra 'חלל' teaches a limit. The other words are simply describing the scene.

steps.title: Why the border and a city of mostly נכרים are excluded
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the משנה's rule. A body near the border or near a city of mostly נכרים is excluded because 'כי ימצא' leaves out places where bodies are commonly found.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if the body was found near the border, or near a city whose majority are נכרים, they do not do עגלה ערופה. This is because it is written 'If one be found', which leaves out places where such things are commonly found.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the משנה and gives the source for one of its rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'כי ימצא', 'if one be found', describe an unusual discovery. Near the border or near a city of mostly נכרים, finding a murdered body is common. So these places are left out of עגלה ערופה.

keyTerms.meaning: This leaves out what is commonly found

phrases.english: If the body was found near the border
or near a city whose majority are non-Jews, and so on.
As it is written: "If one be found" —
this leaves out what is commonly found.
phrases.notes: He means places where murdered bodies turn up often.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא to explaining the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no עגלה ערופה near the border or near a city of mostly נכרים, because bodies are commonly found there.

steps.title: Why we do not measure to a city with no בית דין
steps.stepSummary: A city that has no בית דין is excluded because the פסוק needs 'זקני העיר', the elders of the city, and that city has none.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: or near a city that has no בית דין. This is because we need 'the elders of the city', and there are none.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the next rule in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the 'זקני העיר' of the closest city must take part in the ceremony. A city without a בית דין has no such elders. So it cannot be the city that brings the עגלה ערופה.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ לְעִיר שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ בֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: Or near a city that has no court.
Because we need "the elders of the city",
and there are none there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ לְעִיר שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ בֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the משנה, line by line.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A city with no בית דין is not used for עגלה ערופה, because it has no 'זקני העיר'.

steps.title: Isn't the rule 'measure only to a city with a בית דין' obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to say we measure only to a city with a בית דין. We already know we do not measure to a city without one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: we measure only to a city that has a בית דין. But that is obvious! Since the משנה already taught that we do not measure to a city that has no בית דין, I already know that we measure only to a city that has one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה and challenges it as unneeded. This sets up an answer that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to say the same rule twice. Once it says what is excluded (a city with no בית דין), and once it says what is included (only a city with a בית דין). The גמרא asks what the second line adds, since a משנה does not usually repeat itself for nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: They measure the distance from the body to the nearby cities

phrases.english: They measure only to a city, and so on.
That is obvious!
Since the משנה taught
that we do not measure to a city that has no court,
I already know
that they measure only
to a city that has a court!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the next line of the משנה, using the rule explained in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The line in the משנה: 'אין מודדין אלא לעיר שיש בה בית דין'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The earlier line already excluded a city with no בית דין, so this line seems to add nothing new.

steps.title: Skip the city without a court and measure to the next one
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's words teach a new point, based on a ברייתא. We do not just ignore a city without a בית דין. We pass over it and measure to the nearest city that has one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is teaching us what a ברייתא teaches: How do we know that if the body was found near a city with no בית דין, we skip that city and measure to a city that has a בית דין? The פסוק says 'And the elders of that city shall take', meaning whatever city it ends up being.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 12. The משנה's words are not extra, because they add a practical rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 only taught that a city without a בית דין cannot bring the calf. This step adds what we do next: we keep measuring until we reach a city that has a בית דין. The words 'that city' tell us that city brings the calf even though it is not the closest city.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us (introduces a new point)
As it is taught in a ברייתא
They leave it aside, they skip it
In any case, whatever the situation

steps.whatToRemember: A city without a בית דין is skipped. The measuring continues to the nearest city that has one, and that city brings the עגלה ערופה.

phrases.english: This teaches us, as it is taught in a ברייתא:
From where do we know that if [the body] was found

phrases.aramaic: סָמוּךְ לְעִיר שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ בֵּית דִּין,
phrases.english: close to a city that has no court,
that they leave that city aside

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹדְדִין לְעִיר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ בֵּית דִּין —
phrases.english: and measure to a city that has a court?
The verse states: 'And the elders of that city shall take'
phrases.notes: דברים 21:3

phrases.english: in any case.
phrases.notes: Whichever city the measuring reaches, even one that is not the closest, is 'that city'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12 about why the משנה needs these words.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the words teach a new rule, not a repeat
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words only repeat Step 11: a city without a בית דין does not bring the calf.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words teach that we skip that city and measure on to a city with a בית דין, which then brings the calf.

steps.title: A body found exactly between two cities, and ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה: if the body lies exactly between two cities, רבי אליעזר says each city brings a calf. ירושלים never brings an עגלה ערופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If the body is found exactly between two cities, both cities bring a calf, so there are two calves. These are the words of רבי אליעזר. And ירושלים does not bring an עגלה ערופה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives two rules: what happens when two cities are the same distance away, and that ירושלים is left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally only the single closest city brings the calf. רבי אליעזר says that when there is a true tie, both cities bring one. Separately, ירושלים is excluded even if it is the closest city.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)
The calf whose neck is broken, brought for an unsolved murder

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ נִמְצָא מְכֻוּוֹן בֵּין שְׁתֵּי עֲיָירוֹת —
phrases.english: MISHNAH: If [the body] is found exactly between two cities,
both of them bring two calves,
phrases.notes: Each city brings its own calf.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
And Jerusalem does not bring a calf whose neck is broken.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the body is exactly between two cities, both bring a calf (רבי אליעזר). ירושלים never brings an עגלה ערופה.

steps.title: Head and body found in different places
steps.stepSummary: If the head and body are found apart, רבי אליעזר says the head is brought to the body. רבי עקיבא says the body is brought to the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: If his head was found in one place and his body in another, they bring the head to the body. These are the words of רבי אליעזר. רבי עקיבא says: they bring the body to the head.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a new case. It records a disagreement over which part of the body is moved to the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not say why one part is moved to the other. רבי אליעזר moves the head to where the body lies, and רבי עקיבא moves the body to where the head lies. It might seem to be about measuring, but the גמרא rules that out in step 21, and in step 22 רבי יצחק explains that the dispute is about where to bury him.

phrases.english: If his head was found in one place
and his body in a different place,
they bring the head next to the body,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: הַגּוּף אֵצֶל הָרֹאשׁ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: [they bring] the body next to the head.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִמְצָא רֹאשׁוֹ בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד וְגוּפוֹ בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with another case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: the head is brought to the body. רבי עקיבא: the body is brought to the head.

steps.title: Which point on the body we measure from
steps.stepSummary: Three תנאים disagree about where on the body the measuring starts: the navel, the nose, or the neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where did they measure? רבי אליעזר says: from his navel. רבי עקיבא says: from his nose. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: from the place where he became a חלל, from his neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a disagreement over the exact starting point on the body for measuring the distance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each opinion picks a different part as the center of the person. רבי אליעזר picks the navel and רבי עקיבא picks the nose. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב picks the neck, because that is where the person was killed and became a חלל.
steps.whatToRemember: The three opinions on where to measure from are the navel (רבי אליעזר), the nose (רבי עקיבא) and the neck (רבי אליעזר בן יעקב).

phrases.english: From where would they measure?
Rabbi Eliezer says: from his navel,
Rabbi Akiva says: from his nose,
Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
from the place where he became a slain person, from his neck.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a new question about measuring.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Measuring starts from the navel (רבי אליעזר), the nose (רבי עקיבא), or the neck (רבי אליעזר בן יעקב).

steps.title: Why does רבי אליעזר require two calves?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי אליעזר's ruling that two cities at the same distance each bring a calf.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason of רבי אליעזר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה. It asks why רבי אליעזר rules that both cities bring a calf, and this question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of 'the city that is nearest', which sounds like only one city. So the גמרא wants to know how רבי אליעזר can make two cities bring calves.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא (marks the start of the גמרא's discussion)

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the first ruling of the משנה in Step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why both cities bring a calf when the body is exactly between them.

steps.title: Exact measuring is possible, and 'nearest' can mean more than one city
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds two ideas. A perfectly exact measurement is possible, and the word 'nearest' can also include two nearest cities.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that it is possible to measure exactly. And the word 'nearest' can even mean 'the nearest ones'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by giving two ideas that together explain רבי אליעזר's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, he holds that a real exact tie can be measured, so the case can actually happen. Second, he reads 'nearest' in the פסוק as able to include more than one city, so both tied cities are obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: It is possible to measure exactly

steps.confusionAlert: Both ideas are needed. Without the first, a perfect tie could never be confirmed. Without the second, the פסוק would allow only one city to bring a calf.

phrases.english: He holds that it is possible to measure exactly,
and 'nearest' [can mean] even 'nearest ones'.
phrases.notes: The word is from דברים 21:3. He reads it as covering more than one city.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Exact measuring is possible, and 'nearest' can include two cities.

steps.title: Why ירושלים does not bring an עגלה ערופה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the land was given 'to possess it', and this תנא holds that ירושלים was never divided among the tribes. So it is not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And ירושלים does not bring an עגלה ערופה': because the פסוק says 'to possess it', and this תנא holds that ירושלים was not divided among the tribes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and gives the source for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law of עגלה ערופה applies to land given as a tribe's possession. This תנא holds that ירושלים was never given to any one tribe, so it is not 'possessed' in that sense and is left out of the law.

keyTerms.meaning: Was not divided among the tribes

steps.whatToRemember: ירושלים is excluded from עגלה ערופה because, according to this תנא, it was never given to any tribe as its possession.

phrases.english: 'And Jerusalem does not bring a calf whose neck is broken':
because the verse states 'to possess it',
phrases.notes: דברים 21:1

phrases.english: and he holds that Jerusalem was not divided among the tribes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין יְרוּשָׁלָיִם מְבִיאָה עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next ruling of the משנה and gives its source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ירושלים is excluded from עגלה ערופה because of the word 'to possess it' and because it was not divided among the tribes.

steps.title: What is the head-and-body dispute about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a head found apart from the body and asks what the argument is really about.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If his head was found in one place, etc.' What exactly are they arguing about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the case of the head and body found apart and asks what the two sides are really arguing about. This sets up the next moves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives the two rulings, head to the body or body to the head, but never says what they are for. The גמרא wants to know the practical purpose of moving one part to the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc., short for 'and so on' when quoting

phrases.english: His head was found in one place, etc.
About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the head-and-body dispute from step 15 to find out its purpose.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which law the dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא is about.

steps.title: It cannot be about measuring
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the dispute is about measuring, then rejects that, because the משנה brings up measuring separately afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say they disagree about measuring, that cannot be right. The later part of the משנה asks, 'From where would they measure?' That shows the first part is not about measuring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the obvious answer, that the argument is about where to measure from, and then knocks it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה raises the question of where to measure from in a separate, later clause. If the head-and-body line were already about measuring, that later clause would be repeating itself. So the first clause must be about something else.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion about to be rejected)
The later part of a משנה
The first part of a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the first clause is about measuring just because measuring is the main topic of עגלה ערופה. The גמרא proves the first clause must be about something else.

phrases.english: If you say they disagree about measuring,
but since the later part of the משנה teaches
"From where would they measure,"
it follows that in the first part
we are not dealing with measuring!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to step 20 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the head-and-body dispute is about measuring.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה deals with measuring in a separate later clause, so the first clause would be repeating it.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: the dispute is about burial
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says the argument is about the rule that a מת מצוה is buried in the place where it is found.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: they disagree about the rule that a מת מצוה 'acquires its place.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק gives the real answer. The dispute is about where to bury the body, not about measuring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A body with nobody to take care of it is buried right where it is found. So when the head and body are found apart, we must decide which spot counts as 'his place.' That is the real question in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A dead body with nobody to bury it, so anyone who finds it must bury it
Acquires its place: it is buried where it is found

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
They disagree about the rule that a מת מצוה acquires its place,
phrases.notes: A body nobody is caring for gets buried right where it was found.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20 after step 21 rejected measuring.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is about burying a מת מצוה in its place.

steps.title: Reading the משנה as a burial rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the משנה: a slain person is buried where found, and if the head and body are apart, the two תנאים argue about which part is brought to the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: he is buried in his place. If his head is in one place and his body in another, רבי אליעזר says to bring the head to the body. רבי עקיבא says to bring the body to the head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה again, now according to רבי יצחק's explanation, so the burial meaning is clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same words of the משנה now have a new meaning. 'Bring the head to the body' means bury him where the body lies. 'Bring the body to the head' means bury him where the head lies.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what it means

phrases.english: And this is what it is saying:
For burying him, he acquires his place,
and where his head was found in one place
and his body in another place,
they bring the head next to the body,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: הַגּוּף אֵצֶל הָרֹאשׁ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: the body next to the head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how the משנה reads under רבי יצחק's explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slain מת מצוה is buried where found. רבי אליעזר moves the head to the body, and רבי עקיבא moves the body to the head.

steps.title: Why do they disagree about the burial spot?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind each side's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know the topic is burial, the גמרא asks what idea divides רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree he is buried where he was killed. The question is which part shows the real spot where he fell.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the two rulings in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning behind head-to-body versus body-to-head.

steps.title: Which part moved after the killing?
steps.stepSummary: One view says the body fell in place and the head rolled away. The other says the head fell in place and the body kept going.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds that the body fell where he was killed, and the head rolled away. The other holds that the head fell where it fell, and the body kept running forward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that each side has a different picture of what happened at the moment of the killing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They agree he is buried at the true place of death. רבי אליעזר thinks the body stayed put, so the head is brought to it. רבי עקיבא thinks the body moved on after the head fell, so the body is brought to the head.

phrases.english: One master holds:
phrases.notes: This is רבי אליעזר, who brings the head to the body.

phrases.english: his body fell in its place,
it was the head that rolled and fell elsewhere,
and the other master holds:
phrases.notes: This is רבי עקיבא, who brings the body to the head.

phrases.english: the head fell right where it fell,
it is the body that ran on and kept going.

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים agree a מת מצוה is buried where he was killed. They only argue about which part, the head or the body, marks that spot.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue about whether the head or the body stayed at the true place of death.

steps.title: Why do they disagree about the measuring point?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the next clause of the משנה, where on the body to measure from, and asks the reason behind that dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'From where would they measure?' About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the measuring dispute from step 16 and asks for its reasoning. This sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the topic really is measuring the distance to the nearest city. The גמרא wants the idea behind choosing one body part over another.

phrases.english: "From where would they measure."
About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the burial dispute to the measuring dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning behind measuring from the nose versus the navel.

steps.title: Where is a person's life mainly found?
steps.stepSummary: One view holds that a person's life is mainly in the nose, the other that it is mainly in the navel.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds that a person's life is mainly in his nose. The other holds that it is mainly in his navel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the measuring dispute depends on which body part is the center of a person's life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We measure from the most important part of the person. One side says that is the nose, where breathing happens. The other says it is the navel.

phrases.english: One master holds: the main life is in his nose,
phrases.notes: In the משנה, רבי עקיבא measures from the nose and רבי אליעזר from the navel.

phrases.english: and the other master holds: the main life is in his navel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue about whether a person's life is centered in the nose or in the navel.

steps.title: Is this like the dispute over how an embryo forms?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the measuring dispute matches an older argument among תנאים: does an embryo begin forming from the head? The first view says yes and brings two פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is like the dispute of these תנאים: From where does an embryo begin to form? From its head. As the פסוק says, 'From my mother's womb You pulled me (גוזי),' and another פסוק says, 'Cut off (גזי) your hair and throw it away.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that the nose-versus-navel dispute is the same as an earlier dispute about where an embryo starts forming. It first presents the view that it starts from the head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If life is centered in the head, an embryo would start forming there. The first פסוק uses the word גוזי for birth. The second פסוק uses the same word for cutting hair, which grows on the head, so גוזי is connected to the head.

keyTerms.meaning: Like these תנאים, the same as another dispute
Pulled me out; related to cutting or shearing

phrases.english: Shall we say it is like these תנאים:
From where is an embryo formed?
From its head,
and so the פסוק says:
"From my mother's womb You pulled me",
phrases.notes: תהלים 71:6

phrases.english: and another פסוק says:
"Cut off your hair and throw it away, etc."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 7:29. Here the same word גזי is used for hair, which grows on the head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests that the nose-versus-navel dispute of step 27 matches an earlier dispute among תנאים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the measuring dispute is the same as the dispute about where an embryo starts forming.

steps.title: אבא שאול: the embryo forms from the navel
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול says an embryo begins forming from its navel and sends out its roots from there.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול says: from its navel, and it sends its roots out from there.
steps.whatsHappening: This gives the second side of the embryo dispute, which would match the view that life is centered in the navel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא שאול pictures the navel as a root from which the rest of the body grows. This lines up with the view that measures from the navel, just as the head view lines up with measuring from the nose.

phrases.english: Abba Shaul says: from its navel,
and it sends its roots out from there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the earlier dispute that step 28 began quoting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An embryo begins forming from the navel and grows outward from there.

steps.title: Forming a baby is different from where life sits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on its comparison. אבא שאול only spoke about where an embryo starts forming. About where life sits, everyone agrees it is the nose.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say both views follow אבא שאול. He only said the navel matters for how an embryo forms, since it forms from its middle. But for life itself, everyone agrees it is in the nose, as the פסוק says: 'All in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes back its idea that the measuring dispute is the same as the older argument about embryos.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 28 tried to tie 'measure from the navel' to אבא שאול's view that an embryo forms from the navel. Now the גמרא separates the two questions: where the body starts growing, and where life is found. Since even אבא שאול would agree that life is in the nose, his view does not settle the measuring dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say. The opening for showing that a comparison is not necessary.
He only said his view about this specific matter.
Life, the source of being alive.
Its middle, meaning the navel area.

phrases.english: You can even say that both views follow Abba Shaul,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר אַבָּא שָׁאוּל
phrases.english: Abba Shaul only said his view
regarding the forming of an embryo,
that when an embryo is formed,
it is formed from its middle,
but regarding life,
everyone agrees it is in his nose,
as it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״כׇּל אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁמַת רוּחַ חַיִּים בְּאַפָּיו וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: "All in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life, etc."
phrases.notes: בראשית 7:22

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא אַבָּא שָׁאוּל, עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אֶלָּא לְעִנְיַן יְצִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison made in steps 28 and 29.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the measuring dispute depends on the תנאים' argument about embryos.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It mixes up where an embryo starts forming with where life sits. Those are separate questions.

steps.title: The third view: measure from the neck
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next opinion in the משנה. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says to measure from the neck, the place where the person was killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: measure from the place where he became slain, from his neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up the third opinion in the משנה about where on the body to measure from. It is getting ready to ask for its reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two views measured from the nose or the navel, the places tied to life. This view looks instead at where the killing happened, which it identifies as the neck.

keyTerms.meaning: A slain person, someone who was killed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
From the place where he became slain,
from his neck.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next opinion in the same clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Measure from the neck, where the person was killed.

steps.title: Why the neck?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source behind רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי אליעזר בן יעקב connects being slain to the neck.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other views had reasons about where life sits. This view needs a source showing that 'slain' is linked to the neck.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב?
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the view quoted in step 31.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source linking 'slain' to the neck.

steps.title: A פסוק links the slain to the neck
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in יחזקאל speaks of 'the necks of the slain', which shows that being slain is tied to the neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'To lay you upon the necks of the wicked who are to be slain.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that puts 'necks' and 'slain' together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the פסוק pairs the slain with their necks, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב learns that the neck is the place where a person 'becomes slain'. So that is where the measuring begins.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three places to measure from. רבי עקיבא uses the nose and רבי אליעזר uses the navel, depending on where each holds a person's life is mainly found. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב uses the neck, where the person became slain.

phrases.english: As it is written:
"To lay you upon the necks
of the wicked who are to be slain."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 21:34

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִכְתִיב: לָתֵת אוֹתָךְ אֶל צַוְּארֵי חַלְלֵי רְשָׁעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'the necks of the slain' ties being slain to the neck.

steps.title: The city's elders bring the heifer
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. The זקני ירושלים leave, and the elders of the nearest city bring a heifer that has never pulled a yoke. A blemish does not disqualify it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The זקני ירושלים took their leave and went away. The elders of that city bring a heifer from the cattle that has never pulled a yoke, and a blemish does not disqualify it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts describing the עגלה ערופה ceremony itself, after the measuring is finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The זקני ירושלים's job was only to measure. From here on, the responsibility moves to the elders of the closest city. The heifer must never have been put to work, but a physical blemish does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: A young heifer from the cattle.
A yoke, the frame used to put an animal to work.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The Elders of Jerusalem took their leave
and went away.
The Elders of that city bring

phrases.aramaic: עֶגְלַת בָּקָר אֲשֶׁר לֹא מָשְׁכָה בְּעוֹל,
phrases.english: a heifer from the cattle that has not pulled a yoke,
and a blemish does not disqualify it,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ נִפְטְרוּ זִקְנֵי יְרוּשָׁלָיִם וְהָלְכוּ לָהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The start of a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The city's elders bring an unworked heifer, and a blemish does not disqualify it.

steps.title: Bringing it down to a strong stream
steps.stepSummary: The heifer is brought down to a נחל איתן, meaning a strong-flowing stream. Even a stream that is not strong is valid after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: They bring it down to a stream that is איתן. 'איתן' means what it sounds like: hard, strong. Even if it is not strong, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the place where the heifer is taken and defines the word איתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איתן is understood in its plain sense: forceful or hard. The ideal is a powerful stream, but the משנה adds that a weaker one still works.

keyTerms.meaning: As it sounds, in its plain meaning.

phrases.english: and they bring it down to a stream that is eitan.
Eitan means as it sounds: hard.
phrases.notes: 'Hard' here means forceful, so the stream should have a strong flow.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ אֵיתָן — כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: Even if it is not forceful, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the steps of the ceremony.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A strong stream is preferred, but a weaker one is valid.

steps.title: Breaking the neck, and the rules for the land
steps.stepSummary: The heifer's neck is broken from behind with a cleaver. Afterward, that spot may not be sown or worked, but combing flax or cutting stones there is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: They break its neck from behind with a cleaver. Its place is forbidden to be sown or worked, but it is permitted to comb flax there and to cut stones there.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes how the heifer is killed and what the land may be used for afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban is on farming the ground: sowing it or working the soil. Jobs that are only done on top of the land and do not farm it, like combing flax or cutting stones, are still allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: They break the neck from the back.
A cleaver, a heavy chopping knife.

phrases.english: And they break its neck
with a cleaver from behind.
And its place is forbidden to be sown or worked,
but it is permitted to comb flax there
and to cut stones there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ceremony with the killing of the heifer and the land rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The neck is broken from behind with a cleaver. The land may not be farmed, but non-farming work is allowed.

steps.title: The elders wash their hands and declare
steps.stepSummary: The city's elders wash their hands where the heifer was killed and say, 'Our hands did not spill this blood, and our eyes did not see.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The Elders of that city wash their hands in water at the place where the heifer's neck was broken, and they say: 'Our hands did not spill this blood, nor did our eyes see.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes the elders washing their hands and saying the declaration from the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the high point of the ceremony. The wording of the declaration sounds strange coming from respected judges, and the משנה will question it next.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where the neck was broken.

phrases.aramaic: זִקְנֵי אוֹתָהּ הָעִיר רוֹחֲצִין אֶת יְדֵיהֶן בַּמַּיִם
phrases.english: The Elders of that city wash their hands in water
at the place where the heifer's neck was broken,

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹמְרִים ״יָדֵינוּ לֹא שָׁפְכוּ אֶת הַדָּם הַזֶּה
phrases.english: and they say: "Our hands did not spill this blood
nor did our eyes see."
phrases.notes: דברים 21:7

steps.triggerLanguage: זִקְנֵי אוֹתָהּ הָעִיר רוֹחֲצִין אֶת יְדֵיהֶן בַּמַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ceremony with the washing and the declaration.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The elders wash their hands at the spot and say the declaration from the פסוק.

steps.title: Would anyone suspect the judges of murder?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks why the elders would need to say this. Nobody imagines that the judges of the court are killers.
steps.simpleTranslation: But would it enter our minds that the elders of the court are murderers?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks a sharp question about the declaration. This sets up its explanation of what the elders really mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the words are read simply, the elders are denying a murder that nobody suspected them of. That makes the declaration seem pointless, so its meaning must be something deeper.

keyTerms.meaning: But would it enter our minds? A way of saying the idea is unthinkable.

phrases.english: But would it enter our minds

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁזִּקְנֵי בֵּית דִּין שׁוֹפְכֵי דָּמִים הֵן?
phrases.english: that the elders of the court are murderers?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי עַל דַּעְתֵּינוּ עָלְתָה שֶׁזִּקְנֵי בֵּית דִּין שׁוֹפְכֵי דָּמִים הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the meaning of the declaration in step 37.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the elders' declaration really means, since nobody suspects them of murder.

steps.title: They mean they did not neglect him
steps.stepSummary: The elders are declaring that they did not send the victim away without food or let him leave without an escort.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they mean: he did not come to us and then we sent him away without food, and we did not see him and then leave him without an escort.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains that the declaration is about indirect blame: not caring for a traveler.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not giving a traveler food, or letting him go off alone, could lead to his death. The elders declare that they did not fail in these duties, so they are not even indirectly responsible.

keyTerms.meaning: Escorting a person on his way.

steps.whatToRemember: The elders' declaration is not about murder. It means the city took care of the traveler, giving him food and an escort.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'our hands did not spill' as denying a murder. The משנה says it means denying neglect.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches how much responsibility a community has to look after a guest or traveler who passes through.

phrases.english: Rather, they mean that he did not come to us
and then we sent him off (without food),
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets and some don't.

phrases.english: and we did not see him and then leave him (without an escort).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא בָּא עַל יָדֵינוּ וּפְטַרְנוּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 38.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The declaration means the elders did not neglect the victim by sending him off without food or an escort.
